chapter11.title: Chapter Eleven: Devolved Government
chapter11.summary: Chapter Eleven creates county governments, sets out why power was devolved, and explains how each county's assembly and executive work.

articles.title: Objects of devolution
articles.plain: Explains why power was devolved: to make government democratic and accountable, let people govern themselves and take part in decisions, protect minorities and marginalised groups, bring services closer to people, share resources fairly across Kenya, and add checks and balances.

articles.title: Principles of devolved government
articles.plain: Sets the ground rules for counties: they must be democratic with separate powers for the assembly and the executive, they must have reliable sources of money, and no more than two-thirds of the members of any county body may be of the same gender.

articles.title: County governments
articles.plain: Every county has a county government made up of two parts: the County Assembly and the County Executive. Each county should also spread its services out to local areas where that works well.

articles.title: Membership of county assembly
articles.plain: Sets out who sits in the County Assembly: one member elected from each ward, extra nominated members to meet the gender rule and to represent groups such as people with disabilities and youth, and the Speaker. Members serve five-year terms.
articles.nyamira: Nyamira has 20 wards, so 20 elected MCAs sit in the County Assembly, together with nominated members.

articles.title: Speaker of county assembly
articles.plain: The County Assembly elects its Speaker from people who are not MCAs. The Speaker presides over sittings.
articles.nyamira: Nyamira's Speakership has been disputed since the Speaker was impeached in late 2024. In June 2025 the High Court found the former Speaker had ceased to hold office, but cases have continued.

articles.title: County executive committees
articles.plain: County executive power belongs to the County Executive Committee: the Governor, the Deputy Governor, and members the Governor appoints with the Assembly's approval. Those members cannot be MCAs, and their number is capped by the size of the Assembly.

articles.title: County governor and deputy county governor
articles.plain: The Governor is elected directly by the county's voters on general election day, with the Deputy Governor as running mate. A person can be Governor for at most two terms.

articles.title: Removal of a county governor
articles.plain: A Governor can be removed for gross violation of the Constitution or the law, a serious crime, abuse of office or gross misconduct, or physical or mental incapacity. The process is set by national law: the County Assembly votes to impeach and the Senate decides.
articles.nyamira: In November 2025 the County Assembly voted to impeach Governor Amos Nyaribo. In December 2025 the Senate upheld his objection to the process, so he stayed in office.

articles.title: Vacancy in the office of county governor
articles.plain: Says when the Governor's office becomes vacant (for example death, resignation or removal) and that the Deputy Governor then takes over for the rest of the term.
articles.nyamira: In December 2020 Governor John Nyagarama died in office, and Deputy Governor Amos Nyaribo was sworn in as Governor under this article.

articles.title: Functions of county executive committees
articles.plain: The County Executive Committee carries out county laws and national laws in the county, runs the county departments, may propose laws, and must report fully and regularly to the County Assembly.

articles.title: Urban areas and cities
articles.plain: National law sets how towns and cities are classified and governed, and must give residents a say in running them.

articles.title: Legislative authority of county assemblies
articles.plain: Gives the County Assembly the power to make county laws on the county's functions, to oversee the County Executive, and to approve plans and policies on county resources and infrastructure.

articles.title: Respective functions and powers of national and county governments
articles.plain: Divides public functions between the national and county governments according to the Fourth Schedule. Any function not given to counties belongs to the national government.

articles.title: Transfer of functions and powers between levels of government
articles.plain: A function can be moved from one level of government to the other by agreement, if the other level can do it better. The money to do it must move with it.

articles.title: Boundaries of counties
articles.plain: County boundaries can only be changed on the recommendation of an independent commission, with the approval of both houses of Parliament.

articles.title: Cooperation between national and county governments
articles.plain: The national and county governments must respect each other, consult and help each other, and try to settle disputes through negotiation or mediation before going to court.

articles.title: Support for county governments
articles.plain: Parliament must make sure counties have the support they need. National law can allow the national government to step in when a county cannot do its job or does not manage money properly.

articles.title: Conflict of laws
articles.plain: When a national law and a county law conflict on a shared function, this article decides which one wins. National law prevails in set cases, for example where the country needs one standard; otherwise the county law prevails.

articles.title: Suspension of a county government
articles.plain: The President can suspend a county government only in an emergency or exceptional circumstances, only after an independent inquiry, and only with the Senate's approval. A suspension lasts at most 90 days.

articles.title: Qualifications for election as member of county assembly
articles.plain: Sets who can stand for election as an MCA: a registered voter who meets the educational, moral and ethical requirements, nominated by a party or standing as an independent with enough supporters in the ward. Some people, such as public officers, cannot stand.

articles.title: Vacation of office of member of county assembly
articles.plain: Sets when an MCA loses their seat, for example by death, resignation, missing eight sittings without the Speaker's written permission, leaving the party they were elected on, or being removed under the leadership and integrity rules.
articles.nyamira: In July 2025 the Speaker declared ten MCAs' seats vacant for missing sittings. The High Court suspended that decision with interim orders a few days later.

articles.title: County assembly power to summon witnesses
articles.plain: The County Assembly and its committees can summon anyone to give evidence or produce documents, with the same powers as the High Court to make them comply.

articles.title: Public participation and county assembly powers, privileges and immunities
articles.plain: The County Assembly must do its work in the open: sittings and committee meetings are public, and it must help the public take part in making laws and other business. The public and media can only be excluded for strong, stated reasons.
articles.nyamira: See our lesson on taking part: how to attend Assembly sittings and give your views.

articles.title: County assembly gender balance and diversity
articles.plain: No more than two-thirds of the members of a County Assembly or County Executive Committee may be of the same gender. Parliament must also protect minorities and diversity within counties.

articles.title: County government during transition
articles.plain: National law sets how a county is run during the period when a new County Assembly or Governor is being elected.

articles.title: Publication of county legislation
articles.plain: A county law does not take effect until it is published in the Kenya Gazette.

articles.title: Legislation on Chapter
articles.plain: Parliament must make the laws needed to put this chapter into practice. The main one is the County Governments Act, 2012.

fourthSchedule.title: Fourth Schedule, Part 2: What the county government is responsible for
fourthSchedule.summary: The Fourth Schedule divides public services between the national government and county governments. Part 2 lists the county's functions. If a service is on this list, the county is responsible for it.

functions.title: Agriculture
functions.covers: Crop and animal husbandry, livestock sale yards, county abattoirs, plant and animal disease control, fisheries

functions.title: County health services
functions.covers: County health facilities and pharmacies, ambulance services, primary health care, licensing of food businesses, cemeteries, refuse removal

functions.title: Pollution and nuisances
functions.covers: Control of air pollution, noise pollution, other public nuisances and outdoor advertising

functions.title: Culture and public amenities
functions.covers: Cultural activities, public entertainment, sports and cultural facilities, libraries, museums

functions.title: County transport
functions.covers: County roads, street lighting, traffic and parking, public road transport, ferries and harbours

functions.title: Animal control and welfare
functions.covers: Licensing of dogs, facilities for animal care and burial

functions.title: Trade development and regulation
functions.covers: Markets, trade licences, fair trading, local tourism, cooperative societies

functions.title: County planning and development
functions.covers: Statistics, land survey and mapping, boundaries and fencing, housing, electricity and gas reticulation

functions.title: Pre-primary education and village polytechnics
functions.covers: Pre-primary (ECDE), village polytechnics, homecraft centres and childcare facilities

functions.title: Natural resources and environment
functions.covers: Carrying out specific national policies on natural resources and environmental conservation, including soil and water conservation and forestry

functions.title: County public works and services
functions.covers: Storm water management, water and sanitation services

functions.title: Community participation
functions.covers: Ensuring and coordinating the participation of communities and locations in governance at the local level
